title: AI Specialist Diagnosis and Treatment Resources - Ophthalmology Model
summary: ChatZOC pilots offer ophthalmic consultations, screening support, and teaching tools, with improved clinical access and outcomes as intended benefits.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center describes a specialist model for knowledge questions, diagnostic assistance, and teaching. Pilots are reported across regions of China. The submission claims that the approach can improve access and support clinicians, but it supplies no measured clinical improvement or individual health outcome.
purpose: Support ophthalmic diagnosis, education, and remote access to expertise.

ratings.reason: ChatZOC pilots across China are described without measured clinical or teaching improvements.
Improved diagnosis and patient care are intended benefits, with no measured health improvement supplied.
Narrowing urban-rural healthcare gaps is an intended benefit.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 15: AI Specialist Diagnosis and Treatment Resources - Ophthalmology Model

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: ChatZOC extends ophthalmology information and decision support
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
